The narrowed runs sweep one surface: `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://localhost:6017 --only=chat-reconnect-gap --allow-backend` writes `gap/` and `restored/` in all twelve palettes (24 frames), and `--only=restored-running --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight` writes the two brand palettes of the running state (2 frames). The cause is main's `ce5fd9578` (`<button w-full>` -> `<div class="flex h-8 gap-1"><button min-w-0 grow>`), which this branch's fold kept in the ENABLED path while the withdrawn path went on returning a bare button - correct against this branch's base, wrong against main. The withdrawn pair was re-shot with a conversation OPEN as well as at rest, in both themes, on both trees (see `pinsPass.byteIdentity`); the focus half of the reveal was measured rather than cited from the class list (`pinsPass.checks`).
remediationRecord.qaRoundNineSceneInstrument: QA ROUND 9 ON THE ROUND-8 INSTRUMENT, and the finding of the round that was MAJOR. Q9-1: the focus-reveal block added in design round 8 focused the LAST conversation row, which made the browser scroll the region (`scrollTop 1075` on a 40-conversation store), and the press below then aimed at `pins[0]`'s STORED box - 416px above the viewport, `elementFromPoint` answering null - so the write never reached the backend and four checks failed for a reason of the scene's own making. The fix: the caret row and the press row are both taken from the rows ALREADY inside the region's window (a hoisted `visibleUnpinnedRows` plus a new `whollyInside`, so a partially visible row cannot make the browser scroll as the caret lands), the caret is moved by a REAL CDP Tab from the row's own button, the pin that is read is the one the CARET holds rather than one at an index, and the region is read back and asserted unchanged. The press reads what a click at its point would ACT on (the U3 instrument) before pressing. A/B on one rig, one daemon and one 40-conversation store: pre-fix scene 21 passed / 4 failed; fixed scene 84 / 0; fixed scene with only the focus block removed 76 / 0. And because a scene change can move the pixels it photographs: the pre-fix and fixed scenes were both run against the same daemon and the same 4-conversation store, and 12 of the 13 frames are byte-identical, the thirteenth differing by 66 pixels in one `2x33` box at `1098,1531` - the composer's caret, the same box this file's `reproducibility` field records. AND THE CHECK DISCRIMINATES, by a named mutation rather than by argument: with the pin control's `group-focus-within:opacity-100` removed from `chat-sidebar.tsx` (a hover-only control) and the app rebuilt, the same scene on the same 40-conversation store reports 49 passed / 1 failed, and the failing reading is the focus check with EVERY opacity `0` while the caret is verifiably ON the pin (`{"onButton":true,"inRow":true}` then `{"onPin":true,"subject":"Pin “Sweep 035”"}`) - so what fails is the reveal and not the instrument, which is the property the round asked for. The source edit was reverted and the tree rebuilt before this commit.

citationConvention: WHAT `head`, `partialCapture.refreshedAtHead` and `partialCapture.addedAtHead` NAME, and WHICH RECORD A FOLD TAKES FROM WHICH SIDE - both stated once here because each fold used to restate them around a SHA of its own and every restatement went stale. The three fields name the git HEAD at the MOMENT OF CAPTURE, with the frames themselves still uncommitted in the working tree (the run discloses that in its own `dirtyWorkingTree` field); that is why a frame's measurement in the README can be produced from a commit later than the cite. `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are the other kind of field and name the shipping tree. WHEN MAIN AND THIS BRANCH BOTH REWRITE THIS FILE, THE MERGE IS A PER-FIELD DECISION AND NOT "KEEP MAIN'S RECORD", and it is per FIELD rather than per entry for the same reason: a union taken at entry granularity silently replaces an authored field inside an entry both sides have, which is how this branch's `why` clauses on `supplementary[wake-live-app]` and `supplementary[browser-pane-live]` vanished on the ninth fold (round 8, R8-2). The five groups, numbered as the rig's copy of this rule numbers them so the two homes cannot drift: (1) `head`, `headNote` and the `partialCapture` fields that DESCRIBE a pass - `refreshedAt`, `refreshedAtHead`, `refreshedFromHead`, `addedAt`, `addedAtHead`, `addedFrames`, `note`, `passScopeNote` and every per-pass `*Note` - are THIS branch's, because main's values name main's pass and taking them sends a verifier to a tree that does not carry this branch's frames; (2) the fields that LIST what both sides touched - `supplementary`'s ENTRIES, and `refreshedStories`, `refreshedThemes`, `addedSurfaces` - are the UNION of the two sides' entries or values, because the merged tree carries both and either side's list alone would claim a pass that did not run in it; (3) INSIDE a `supplementary` entry that exists on both sides, this pass's AUTHORED keys - `why`, `capturedAt`, `capturedAtHead` and any note - are KEPT and only the listings are unioned, since an entry is a record this branch wrote rather than a listing; (4) `refreshedFrames` is RE-DERIVED against HEAD rather than added up, and `frames`, `surfaces`, `themes`, `countsMean`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are re-derived from the merged tree and taken from neither side - `countsMean` belongs here because it restates `frames`/`surfaces`, and its prose says what each field counts and where to read it rather than carrying a number of its own; (5) NO FIELD THAT SPELLS OUT WHAT A CITATION NAMES is carried from main's side under any name - main's manifest still has `refreshedAtHeadNote`, the spelling this branch deleted, and carrying main's keys this branch lacks re-introduces it. Group (5) is stated once, here: earlier passes restated it in two more places in this field, which is the duplication round 9's R9-1 filed, and deleting them rather than re-pointing them is the same treatment the counts and the `why` clauses got. THE GATE'S TWO HALVES, named so the blind spot is auditable rather than summarised: `check-evidence.mjs` asks whether a citation RESOLVES (`citationFailures`) and whether it is an ANCESTOR OF `HEAD` (`citationAncestryFailures` - named by symbol rather than by line, since a line number is one more thing a later pass has to keep true). Main's own commit satisfies both, which is why the round-6 defect was invisible to it - and neither half asks whether the tree a citation names carries the frames this record declares. TWO CORRECTIONS THIS RULE NEEDED ONCE IT WAS EXERCISED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED, both found by the ninth fold: `countsMean` was listed in BOTH the keep-this-branch's group and the re-derive group, and a resolver reading the first one carried a stale prose count past a fold that had moved `frames`; and main's citation notes came back through the "carry main's keys this branch lacks" step, which is why group (5) exists.
